modules.title: Data Privacy
modules.purpose: To ensure advanced housekeeping supervisors understand and execute Aurelle Hotels & Residences data privacy policies, protecting guest and employee personal information.
modules.completion_criteria: Successful completion of training within Week 1, task execution, and passing the data privacy assessment.

content.text: Master the principles of purpose limitation, identity document handling, and retention periods for guest data.
Comply with storage, transmission, and prohibition rules regarding personal devices, removable media, and employee personnel files.
Identify data security incidents and execute mandatory reporting procedures within the required timeframe.

content.activity: Complete Guest Data Privacy training

content.description: Review housekeeping operational workflows to ensure no guest identity documents or personal files are stored on personal mobile phones, shared drives, or USB drives.
content.expected_outcome: Confirmation that all data handling complies with Aurelle privacy policies.
content.completion_criteria: Audit report verifying zero prohibited data storage on personal devices or shared drives.

content.situation: A caller phones the housekeeping department asking if a specific guest is currently staying at the property and requests their room number.
expected_actions: Refuse to disclose the room number or guest name to the caller.
Connect the call to the room without confirming the guest's presence.

content.question: Within what timeframe must Guest Data Privacy training be completed?
content.explanation: Guest Data Privacy training must be completed within Week 1.

options: To deliver the guest's stay or for a documented business need
content.question: For what purpose may guest personal data be accessed?
content.explanation: Guest personal data may only be accessed to deliver the guest's stay or for a documented business need.

options: Scanned into the PMS and paper copies retained
Scanned only into the PMS; paper copies are prohibited
content.question: How should a guest's passport or national ID be scanned?
content.explanation: A guest's passport or national ID may be scanned only into the PMS; paper copies are prohibited.

options: No later than 7 days after check-out
content.question: When must scanned copies of guest identity documents be permanently deleted from the PMS?
content.explanation: Scanned copies of guest identity documents must be permanently deleted from the PMS no later than 7 days after check-out.

options: By the end of the shift
content.question: Within what timeframe must any suspected loss or disclosure of guest data be reported?
content.explanation: Any suspected loss or disclosure of guest data must be reported to the Duty Manager and IT within 1 hour of discovery.

content.question: Employee personal files may be stored in shared drives if access is restricted to department managers.
content.explanation: Employee personal files must be accessed only by Human Resources and stored in the HR system, never in shared drives.

rubric.criterion: Understanding of Data Handling and Retention
rubric.pass_condition: Achieves full score on data retention and handling questions.
rubric.expected_performance: Correctly identifies PMS scanning rules, 7-day retention limits, and prohibition of personal device storage.

rubric.pass_condition: Accurately details reporting channels and timeframes.
rubric.expected_performance: Demonstrates correct protocol for reporting data incidents within 1 hour and handling caller inquiries.

modules.title: Fire & Life Safety
modules.purpose: To ensure all employees at Aurelle Muscat Bay understand emergency procedures, fire assembly points, the RACE protocol, and extinguisher operation.
modules.completion_criteria: Completion of Day 1 fire orientation, passing all quiz questions, and successful demonstration of extinguisher PASS technique.

content.text: Complete first-day fire and life safety orientation and locate work area assembly points and fire exits.
Execute the RACE procedure correctly upon hearing the fire alarm and avoid using lifts.
Demonstrate practical extinguisher use with the PASS technique and participate in scheduled fire drills.

content.activity: Complete Fire and Life Safety orientation

content.description: Demonstrate correct use of a fire extinguisher using the PASS technique during practical training.
content.expected_outcome: Successful operation of the extinguisher utilizing Pull, Aim, Squeeze, Sweep.
content.completion_criteria: Completion of practical demonstration evaluated during Week 2.

content.situation: You are on the housekeeping floor when the fire alarm sounds. Guests are panicking near the elevators, and smoke is detected down the corridor.
expected_actions: Recall and follow the RACE procedure (Rescue, Alarm, Contain, Evacuate).
Ensure no one attempts to use the lifts.
Guide guests toward the two nearest fire exits and direct them to the fire assembly point.

options: Before the end of the probationary period
content.question: When must the Fire and Life Safety orientation be completed?
content.explanation: Fire and Life Safety orientation must be completed on Day 1.

content.question: Every new employee must attend a fire and life safety orientation on their first day.
content.explanation: Every new employee must attend a fire and life safety orientation on their first day.

options: The names of all housekeeping staff
The location of the fire assembly point and the two nearest fire exits
content.question: What must employees know regarding their work area?
content.explanation: Employees must know the location of the fire assembly point and the two nearest fire exits for their work area.

options: Follow the PASS procedure and use the lifts for speed
Follow the RACE procedure and must not use the lifts
Evacuate immediately using the lifts and ignore alarms
Rescue, Contain, and use lifts for heavy equipment evacuation
content.question: Upon hearing the fire alarm, what procedure must employees follow, and what equipment must they avoid?
content.explanation: On hearing the fire alarm, employees must follow the RACE procedure (Rescue, Alarm, Contain, Evacuate) and must not use the lifts.

content.question: How often must all employees participate in a fire drill?
content.explanation: All employees must participate in a fire drill every six months.

content.question: Which staff members must demonstrate correct use of a fire extinguisher using the PASS technique during practical training?
content.explanation: Supervisory and engineering staff must demonstrate correct use of a fire extinguisher using the PASS technique during practical training.

rubric.pass_condition: 100% accurate identification during facility walk-through.
rubric.expected_performance: Employee accurately identifies assembly points and the two nearest fire exits.

rubric.pass_condition: Flawless verbal and situational recitation of RACE.
rubric.expected_performance: Employee correctly explains and demonstrates steps for Rescue, Alarm, Contain, and Evacuate without using lifts.

rubric.pass_condition: Successful demonstration of Pull, Aim, Squeeze, and Sweep.
rubric.expected_performance: Supervisory staff member performs the PASS technique correctly during practical session.

modules.title: HR Operations
modules.purpose: To equip Aurelle Muscat Bay supervisors with advanced operational knowledge regarding probation, working hours, attendance policies, grievance escalation, and leave management.
key_concepts: Annual leave accrual and carry-forward rules
assessment_topics: HR Operations and Leave Policy Compliance
modules.completion_criteria: Successful completion of all checklist tasks, quizzes with a passing grade, and completion of the 30-day check-in requirement.

content.text: Understand probation timelines, 30-day check-ins, working hours, and absence and grievance reporting protocols.
Navigate internal transfer eligibility, annual leave accruals, carry-forwards, submission notices, blackout dates, and medical certificate requirements.

content.activity: Review probation and initial HR policy requirements upon onboarding
Complete the 30-day check-in meeting with the reporting manager and record it in the HR portal
Acknowledge standard working hours and overtime pre-approval rules
Acknowledge illness absence reporting procedure
Acknowledge annual leave accrual entitlements

content.description: Schedule, execute, and document your 30-day check-in meeting with your reporting manager in the HR portal.
content.expected_outcome: A fully recorded check-in entry inside the HR portal meeting compliance with onboarding check-in milestones.
content.completion_criteria: The meeting record timestamp is successfully logged in the HR portal before D30.

content.situation: A housekeeping team member approaches you wishing to formally complain about roster allocations. They want to know the exact path for raising and escalating their grievance.
expected_actions: Instruct the employee to raise the grievance first with their direct supervisor
Inform them that if the grievance is unresolved within five working days, it must be escalated in writing to Human Resources

options: Three months, with reviews at month one and two
Six months, with formal reviews at the end of months one, three and five
One year, with a review every quarter
Six months, with a formal review only at the end of probation
content.question: What is the duration of the probation period for new employees, and when do formal reviews take place?
content.explanation: New employees must complete a six-month probation period, with formal reviews at the end of months one, three and five.

content.question: Standard working time is 48 hours per week across six shifts, and overtime must be approved in advance by the department head.
content.explanation: Standard working time is 48 hours per week across six shifts; overtime is required to be approved in advance by the department head.

options: At least 30 minutes before shift start
At least one hour before shift start
At least two hours before the start of the shift
By the end of the shift day
content.question: How much advance notice must be given when reporting an absence due to illness?
content.explanation: Absence due to illness must be reported to the supervisor at least two hours before the start of the shift.

options: Maximum of 10 days; lapse on 31 December
Maximum of 5 days; lapse on 31 March
Maximum of 5 days; lapse on 31 December
No days may be carried forward
content.question: What is the maximum number of unused annual leave days that may be carried forward, and when do excess days lapse?
content.explanation: A maximum of 5 unused annual leave days may be carried forward to the next year; any excess days lapse on 31 March.

content.question: How far in advance must annual leave requests be submitted through the HR portal?
content.explanation: Annual leave requests must be submitted through the HR portal at least 14 days before the first day of leave.

options: Any sick leave requires a medical certificate
Sick leave of more than two consecutive days must be supported by a medical certificate submitted within 48 hours of return
Medical certificates are only required after five consecutive days
Medical certificates must be submitted before taking sick leave
content.question: What is the rule regarding sick leave certificates?
content.explanation: Sick leave of more than two consecutive days must be supported by a medical certificate submitted within 48 hours of return.

content.topic: HR Operations and Leave Policy Compliance

rubric.pass_condition: Successfully logs 30-day check-in and articulates review timelines.
rubric.expected_performance: Demonstrates thorough understanding of the 6-month probation milestones and logs the 30-day check-in correctly.

rubric.pass_condition: Accurately identifies reporting times and pre-approval workflows.
rubric.expected_performance: Applies correct overtime pre-approval rules and 2-hour illness absence reporting.

rubric.pass_condition: Describes the accurate timeline and sequence for escalating grievances.
rubric.expected_performance: Correctly follows the two-tier grievance process including direct supervisor review and 5-day HR escalation.

rubric.pass_condition: Resolves complex leave scheduling scenarios in compliance with LVP-01.
rubric.expected_performance: Correctly manages leave accruals, 14-day advance notices, blackout date exceptions, and medical certificate rules.

modules.title: Company Orientation and 2 related areas
modules.purpose: To orient advanced housekeeping staff on company conduct, safety protocols, escalation procedures, and handbook guidelines at Aurelle Muscat Bay.
key_concepts: Chemical and power tool PPE requirements
assessment_topics: Company Orientation, Safety and Conduct Standards
modules.completion_criteria: Successful completion of all Day 1 checklist items, tasks, scenarios, and achieving a passing grade on the quiz and assessment.

content.text: Comply with Aurelle uniform, personal protective equipment, and manual handling standards.
Execute media escalation protocols and complete employee handbook and culture requirements.

content.activity: Read the Employee Handbook and sign the acknowledgement form
Complete the Aurelle Culture e-learning path

content.description: Sign and submit your Employee Handbook acknowledgement form to your HR Executive during orientation.
content.expected_outcome: Signed acknowledgement form collected by HR on your first working day.
content.completion_criteria: Acknowledgement form physically or digitally signed and handed to HR Executive.

content.situation: While supervising a room deep-clean, a housekeeper needs to move a heavy equipment crate weighing 25 kg. Simultaneously, a journalist approaches you in the lobby asking about a recent maintenance incident.
expected_actions: Instruct the team to use two people or a trolley for the 25 kg load since it is heavier than 20 kg.
Refuse to speak to the journalist about the incident.
Refer all media enquiries immediately to the Communications team.

options: Casual professional clothing and a badge
The full Aurelle uniform and name badge, following Annex A grooming standards
Personal attire with safety footwear only
content.question: What items must employees wear while on duty according to the Code of Workplace Conduct?
content.explanation: Employees must wear the full Aurelle uniform and name badge while on duty, following the grooming standard in Annex A.

content.question: Which protective items must be worn when handling cleaning chemicals or using power tools? (Select all that apply)
content.explanation: Safety footwear, gloves and eye protection must be worn when handling cleaning chemicals or using power tools.

content.question: Loads heavier than 20 kg must be lifted by two people or moved with a trolley.
content.explanation: Loads heavier than 20 kg must be lifted by two people or moved with a trolley.

options: Provide an off-the-record summary to build good public relations
Answer only factual questions about the housekeeping department
Refuse to speak to the media about any incident and refer all enquiries to the Communications team
Escalate the reporter directly to the hotel General Manager for an immediate interview
content.question: An external news reporter approaches you in the hallway regarding an operational incident. What must you do?
content.explanation: Employees must not speak to the media about any incident and must refer all enquiries to the Communications team.

content.question: When must all employees read the Employee Handbook and sign the acknowledgement form?
content.explanation: All employees must read the Employee Handbook and sign the acknowledgement form on their first working day.

content.question: What is the recommended timeframe for new employees to complete the Aurelle Culture e-learning path?
content.explanation: New employees are encouraged to complete the Aurelle Culture e-learning path within their first 30 days.

content.topic: Company Orientation, Safety and Conduct Standards

rubric.pass_condition: Demonstrates 100% adherence to uniform and PPE standards.
rubric.expected_performance: Wears full Aurelle uniform with name badge and correctly uses safety footwear, gloves, and eye protection during chemical/tool tasks.

rubric.pass_condition: Correctly identifies and manages heavy loads without violating weight limits.
rubric.expected_performance: Applies the two-person lift or trolley rule for loads exceeding 20 kg.

rubric.pass_condition: Accurately routes simulated media inquiries and submits signed acknowledgement documentation.
rubric.expected_performance: Successfully refers media enquiries to the Communications team and completes handbook sign-off on Day 1.

modules.title: Housekeeping Operations
modules.purpose: To provide advanced housekeeping supervisors with operational standards, inspection protocols, health and safety procedures, and guest service guidelines at Aurelle Muscat Bay.
key_concepts: Lost and found register and tamper-evident bags
Retention periods for valuables and non-valuables
modules.completion_criteria: Complete all checklist items, successfully finish the practical inspection task, resolve the welfare check scenario, and achieve a minimum score of 80% on the quiz and practical assessment.

content.text: Master room cleaning inspection standards, defect logging timeframes, and DND welfare check protocols.
Implement strict lost and found logging, valuation handling, retention periods, and claim verification procedures.
Execute pre-shift responsibilities, chemical handling compliance, uniform protocols, and team break guidelines.

content.activity: Complete Chemical Handling training before first use of cleaning or pool chemicals
Acknowledge check-out room 42-point cleaning and PMS release standards
Acknowledge supervisor minimum inspection quota of 12 rooms per shift
Acknowledge DND handling and Duty Manager escalation rules after 15:00
Acknowledge mandatory two-person welfare check requirements
Acknowledge the 30-minute maintenance logging rule for engineering defects
Acknowledge 1-hour lost & found register logging requirement
Acknowledge tamper-evident bag and security hand-off protocols for valuables
Acknowledge retention periods for non-valuable and valuable items
Acknowledge identity verification and description matching rules for returning items
Acknowledge pre-shift briefing and section allocation duties
Acknowledge uniform laundering through the Uniform Room
Acknowledge staff break location guidelines away from guest areas

content.description: Conduct a mock room inspection session using the room inspection app, identify simulated 42-point defects, log an engineering defect within the required timeframe, and verify check-out room PMS release status.
content.expected_outcome: Demonstrated proficiency in executing supervisor room inspections, logging engineering defects within 30 minutes, and enforcing the 42-point cleaning standard.
content.completion_criteria: Successfully inspect 3 simulated rooms, record all defects via the app, log an engineering defect within 30 minutes, and properly release the rooms.

content.situation: At 15:10, a room on your floor still displays a Do Not Disturb (DND) sign. The guest has not answered phone calls. You need to coordinate a welfare check according to Aurelle standards.
expected_actions: Inform the Duty Manager immediately that the DND sign remains after 15:00.
Ensure the welfare check is performed by exactly two employees.
Ensure one of the two employees conducting the welfare check is the Duty Manager or a Security officer.

content.question: What is the minimum number of rooms a supervisor must inspect per shift using the room inspection app?
content.explanation: Supervisors must inspect a minimum of 12 rooms per shift using the room inspection app and record all defects.

content.question: Engineering defects found during supervisor inspections must be logged in the maintenance system within 30 minutes.
content.explanation: Engineering defects found during inspection must be logged in the maintenance system within 30 minutes.

options: Before the end of the shift
content.question: Within what timeframe must all found items be logged in the Lost & Found register?
content.explanation: All found items must be logged in the Lost & Found register within 1 hour of being found.

options: 30 days for non-valuables and 90 days for valuables
60 days for non-valuables and 120 days for valuables
90 days for non-valuables and 180 days for valuables
180 days for non-valuables and 365 days for valuables
content.question: What are the required retention periods before disposal or donation for non-valuable items and valuables respectively?
content.explanation: Non-valuable items must be kept for 90 days and valuables for 180 days before disposal or donation.

options: Keep them in the supervisor's desk drawer until the guest calls.
Seal them in a tamper-evident bag and hand them to Security in line with the Security SOP.
Log them in the register after 24 hours and store them in the general housekeeping locker.
Hand them directly to the General Manager.
content.question: A room attendant finds a gold watch and cash left behind in a departure room. How must these valuable items be handled?
content.explanation: Valuables, including cash, jewellery, electronics and documents, must be sealed in a tamper-evident bag and handed to Security in line with the Security SOP.

options: At home using delicate wash settings
At a local commercial laundry service
Returned to the Uniform Room for laundering
In the guest laundry facilities on property
content.question: Where should employees launder their work uniforms according to staff guidelines?
content.explanation: Uniforms must be returned to the Uniform Room for laundering; washing uniforms at home is not permitted.

rubric.pass_condition: Zero missed defect logging windows and complete adherence to the 42-point standard.
rubric.expected_performance: Accurately inspects rooms using the app, meets the 12-room quota, and logs engineering defects within 30 minutes.

rubric.pass_condition: Flawless execution of register logging and security handover procedures.
rubric.expected_performance: Logs items within 1 hour, correctly handles valuables with tamper-evident bags, and follows retention and verification rules.

rubric.pass_condition: Demonstrates full compliance with safety protocols, pre-shift allocation, and staff guidelines.
rubric.expected_performance: Completes chemical handling training, conducts pre-shift briefings, coordinates DND welfare checks properly, and enforces break policies.

content.text: Comply with IT access, system levels, mobile device management, and business use restrictions.
Adhere to compliance pass mark rules, coaching review policies, conflict of interest declarations, ID badge protocols, and attendance clocking.

options: They are automatically terminated from their position

options: Immediately upon submission of the request
Only after the Information Security Basics module has been completed
Once the departmental head approves via email

options: They can be connected freely at any time

Only after enrolment in the Mobile Device Management app
Personal devices are strictly prohibited from connecting to staff Wi-Fi under any circumstances

options: Collect from HR on Day 1 and wear it visibly at all times while on property

modules.title: Information Security

key_concepts: Multi-factor authentication for email and PMS
Personal account credentials and screen locking
Phishing reporting and security incident notification
Guest privacy protection on personal social media
modules.completion_criteria: Successful completion of all e-learning requirements, policy acknowledgments in the HR portal, practical tasks, and achieving a passing grade on the knowledge assessment.

content.text: Complete information security basics e-learning and properly acknowledge the Information Security Policy.
Apply secure credential management, password standards, and multi-factor authentication for system access.
Identify and report security threats, suspected phishing, guest privacy breaches, and security incidents according to policy.

content.activity: Acknowledge the Information Security Policy in the HR portal

content.description: Configure system credentials ensuring passwords meet length requirements and multi-factor authentication is active for email and PMS.
content.expected_outcome: Compliant password and active MFA setup prior to accessing property systems.
content.completion_criteria: Password is at least 12 characters and MFA is verified active for email and PMS.

content.situation: While working in the housekeeping back-of-house area, you notice an unusual email asking for urgent credential verification. Additionally, you finish a task on a workstation and need to step away.
expected_actions: Lock the workstation immediately before leaving it unattended.
Report the suspicious email using the Report Phishing button without forwarding it to colleagues.
Report any suspected security incident to the IT Service Desk immediately.

options: Before being granted access to any Aurelle system
Within their first month of employment
Only after a security audit occurs
Within the first week of employment
content.question: When must an employee complete the Information Security Basics e-learning module?
content.explanation: All employees must complete the Information Security Basics e-learning module before being granted access to any Aurelle system.

options: At least 8 characters, changed every 90 days
At least 12 characters long and must be changed immediately if compromise is suspected
At least 10 characters with numbers and symbols, changed annually
No minimum length, but changed whenever prompted by the browser
content.question: What are the core requirements regarding password length and updates under the Information Security Policy?
content.explanation: Passwords must be at least 12 characters long and must be changed immediately if compromise is suspected.

content.question: Multi-factor authentication must be enabled for email and for the Property Management System (PMS) before first use.
content.explanation: Multi-factor authentication must be enabled for email and for the Property Management System (PMS) before first use.

options: Forward the email to your supervisor and team members as a warning
Delete it immediately without notifying anyone
Report it using the Report Phishing button and do not forward it to colleagues
Reply to the sender asking for clarification
content.question: You receive a suspected phishing email while on shift. What is the correct action to take?
content.explanation: Suspected phishing emails must be reported using the Report Phishing button and must not be forwarded to colleagues.

options: Yes, if no guests are visible in the photographs

Declare any unsolicited guest gifts above USD 25 to the Duty Manager within 24 hours
